description:
## What

Both PKIX-jy95.* (pkix-policy-zlint / pkix-policy-pkilint runtime adapters) and PKIX-hbzo.1 (pkix-difftest using zlint+pkilint as differential oracles) need substantially the same plumbing:

- Subprocess spawn / args / stdin / stdout / stderr / exit-code handling
- JSON / NDJSON parsing of upstream output
- Mapping of upstream verdict vocabularies to workspace types
- Error handling for missing binary / version mismatch / malformed output

## Options

- **A) Shared infrastructure crate.** New `pkix-zlint-bridge` and `pkix-pkilint-bridge` crates that expose 'run zlint on this cert, get parsed findings' as a function. PKIX-jy95.1 (`pkix-policy-zlint`) uses the bridge to expose findings as `Lint` impls; PKIX-hbzo.1 (pkix-difftest oracle) uses the same bridge to get findings for differential comparison. Maximum code reuse; new crate per upstream tool. Workspace bears the bridge maintenance.

- **B) Each crate implements its own subprocess plumbing.** PKIX-jy95.1 has its own subprocess code; PKIX-hbzo.1 has its own. Duplication, but no inter-crate coupling. The bridge logic is small (a few hundred lines) so duplication is bounded.

- **C) Hybrid: bridge crate exists but is dev-only / internal.** Ship the bridge logic as a workspace-internal helper crate (publish=false), consumed by pkix-policy-zlint AND by pkix-difftest's oracle. External consumers can't depend on the bridge directly; they consume pkix-policy-zlint. Minimal external surface, max internal reuse.

## Considerations

- (A) and (C) require deciding the bridge's API shape before either consumer can start.
- (B) means both consumers can proceed independently; we discover code duplication later and refactor if it bites.
- Workspace pattern (looking at pkix-revocation / pkix-revocation-http, pkix-truststore / pkix-truststore-system): typically NO shared 'internal' helper; each pair of crates manages its own subprocess / HTTP details. Suggests (B).
- But: pkix-revocation-http and pkix-revocation-http-oracle (hypothetical) don't currently both exist. The duplication problem is unique to the zlint/pkilint case because BOTH are also differential oracles.

## Decision-gate

Best decided before EITHER PKIX-jy95.1 or PKIX-hbzo.1 implementation starts. Otherwise we'll either commit to (A)/(C) post-hoc (refactor) or end up at (B) by default.

## Cross-references

- PKIX-jy95 parent (the runtime adapter epic)
- PKIX-hbzo.1 (differential oracle bead)
- AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6 (the shared types must be cache-friendly regardless of crate-split choice)
title: Decide code-share between policy-adapter crates and pkix-difftest oracles (shared pkix-zlint-bridge crate?)
